fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Jehoshaphat stationed troops in every fortified city of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:2). Every fortified city, not just a few of them. Not one of them gets left with an empty post.

That's it. The text says the LORD was with Jehoshaphat “…because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David.” (2 Chronicles 17:3). Notice the word earlier. The text says David's earlier ways. Plain and simple, and no troop count needed.

Yes! The text says he “…walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.” (2 Chronicles 17:4). Israel is the same Israel he was strengthening himself against back in verse 1, and he doesn't copy their practices either. He follows God's commandments, not the neighbors.

Moab doesn't come up in this verse. The text says he “…walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.” (2 Chronicles 17:4). Israel is the one named, the same Israel Jehoshaphat was already strengthening himself against (2 Chronicles 17:1).

You got it. The text says he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah (2 Chronicles 17:6). Right before that, the verse says his heart took delight in the ways of the LORD. Those two things sit side by side in the same verse.

Teach is right. Jehoshaphat sent them to teach in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7). With a king who has all those troops, you'd expect a march, but this team went out to teach. Five officials, nine Levites and two priests, and not one of them was sent to fight. That's a whole lot of teachers.

I see why you'd go there, with all those troops around. But the text says Jehoshaphat sent these officials, Levites and priests out to teach in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7). Teaching is the job it gives this team. They went out to teach.

That's the one. The text says they went through the towns of Judah “…taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD.” (2 Chronicles 17:9). The Book went with them. And they taught the people in every one of those towns.

Camels and spices sound like a believable gift, but they aren't in this verse. The Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks (2 Chronicles 17:11). No spice rack, friend. This gift came with hooves.

Horses and chariots aren't in this verse, and Egypt isn't either. Some Philistines brought gifts and silver, and the Arabs brought 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks (2 Chronicles 17:11). The Arabs' gift was livestock, friend.

Markets would make sense with all that tribute coming in, but the verse doesn't say it. Jehoshaphat built fortresses and store cities in Judah (2 Chronicles 17:12). The next verse says he kept vast supplies in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:13).
